column5: Three further fetchers swallow a failed response into an empty result and two of them render an error block that can never execute
column6: Code review issue 34 recorded this pattern in the shared infinite data hook. Reviewing the areas no earlier session had covered finds three more independent fetchers doing the same thing. src/components/Products/ProductDetailPage/ProductFaqSection.tsx:37-49 returns response.data on success and falls off the end after a console.error at :48 so it resolves to undefined - SWR treats a resolved undefined as a SUCCESS so the error value destructured at :53 is never populated and the error block rendered at :94-96 is UNREACHABLE DEAD CODE. src/components/Products/ProductDetailPage/ProductReviewsSection.tsx:28-33 is the same shape with its own dead error block at :109-111. src/views/homePage/HomeBuilder.tsx:36-44 returns null on an unsuccessful response and its callers simply skip the state update - and that component has no error UI at all so a failed home layout fetch falls through to the EmptyState at :103-113 reading Fresh finds on the way. The pattern is therefore present in four independent fetchers and in two of them somebody deliberately wrote an error state that cannot fire.
column10: Any failure of the FAQ or reviews or home layout endpoints - an outage a 500 or a market with no permission to the scope.
column11: 1. Make the product FAQ endpoint fail and open a product page - the FAQ section reports zero FAQs and never shows its error message. 2. Repeat for the reviews endpoint with the same result. 3. Make the home layout endpoint fail and open the home page - it renders the empty state as though the store has no content.
column12: Each failure surfaces the error state its component already contains and the home builder gains one - all distinct from a genuine empty result.
column13: All three render as though the data is legitimately empty and the two written error states never appear.
column14: Outages are invisible on the highest traffic screens. A product looks like it has no reviews and no FAQs and the home page looks like an empty store - which hides incidents and suppresses retries. The two dead error blocks also give a false impression on code review that the case is handled.
column15: Throw from each fetcher when the response is unsuccessful so SWR populates error - which immediately activates the two error blocks that already exist. For HomeBuilder track the failure in state and render an error with a retry rather than falling through to the empty state. Fix the shared hook from issue 34 at the same time so one convention applies everywhere.
